title: Lesson 44 - Decision Drill: Agent API Versus a Standard Channel or a Flow Callout
description: Given a scenario, identify when it's appropriate to use Agent API.

questions.question: A built-in Flow on a case record must have the agent summarize the case and write a field when a rep clicks a button. Which seam fits?
options: An AI Agent action invoked from Flow, because the caller is inside Salesforce and runs under the running user
Agent API with a client credential token
questions.explanation: When the caller is already inside Salesforce, a Flow callout invokes the agent under the running user with no external token, base URL, or session to manage.

questions.question: A customer's own mobile app must embed the agent and pass its signed-in user's identity so that user's access governs. Which approach fits?
options: Agent API with an identity carrying OAuth flow such as token exchange, so the user's identity crosses the boundary
A prompt template with no agent
questions.explanation: An external customer built surface that must propagate a specific user's identity calls for Agent API with a flow that carries that identity rather than a shared service account.

questions.question: A back office service with no user interface must call the agent nightly to triage cases. Which choice fits?
options: Agent API using the client credentials flow, running as a dedicated integration user
A public Service agent on the website
questions.explanation: A headless service invocation with no human is the client credentials pattern on Agent API, running as its own integration identity.
